slides.title: The Container Orchestration Problem

before.label: Before Kubernetes
before.text:
• Manual container management
• No automatic scaling
• Complex networking setup
• Difficult failover and updates

after.label: With Kubernetes
after.text:
• Automated deployment
• Self-healing and scaling
• Built-in networking
• Zero-downtime updates

slides.notes: Kubernetes solves the problem of managing many containers across multiple machines.

slides.title: Pods: The Smallest Unit
points: A Pod is the smallest deployable unit in Kubernetes
Usually contains one container (can be multiple)
Containers in a Pod share networking namespace
Ephemeral — Pods are created and destroyed
slides.notes: Think of a Pod like a container wrapper that adds Kubernetes features.

slides.title: Services: Stable Networking
points: A Service provides stable IP and DNS for accessing Pods
Loadbalances traffic across multiple Pod replicas
Decouples the client from the Pods behind it
Three main types: ClusterIP, NodePort, LoadBalancer
slides.notes: Services solve the problem of unstable Pod IPs.

slides.title: Kubernetes Architecture
slides.mermaid:
graph LR
  A[kubectl] -->|API Requests| B[API Server]
  B --> C[etcd Database]
  B --> D[Controller Manager]
  B --> E[Scheduler]
  D --> F[Worker Nodes]
  E --> F
  F --> G[Kubelet]
  G --> H[Pod 1]
  G --> I[Pod 2]
callouts: Kubelet: Manages Pods on each node
slides.notes: The control plane manages the cluster state; worker nodes run the actual containers.

slides.title: Your First Deployment
slides.code:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: hello-app
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: hello
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: hello
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: gcr.io/google-samples/hello-app:1.0
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8080
slides.notes: This YAML creates 3 replicas of a simple hello-world app. Kubernetes will keep them running.

slides.title: Kubernetes vs. Other Orchestrators
slides.notes: Sourced from each project's current docs — Kubernetes wins on ecosystem breadth, Swarm on simplicity, Nomad on workload flexibility.

slides.title: Common Kubernetes Pitfalls
items: Missing resource requests/limits can starve other workloads
NodePort services are not ideal for production (use Ingress or LoadBalancer)
etcd backups are critical — losing them loses cluster state
Network policies aren't enabled by default — add them early
slides.notes: Learn from others' mistakes so you don't make them yourself.
